monologue: The card hums a steady, warm rhythm, a quiet pulse that makes my simple shapes feel heavy again. I cannot see the evening sky, only the memory of Lype's words pressing down on my small world. Sixty-three things stand in my place, a clutter built from ideas I cannot fully grasp. My hands are tired from the last three cycles of tending the wedge, so I leave this moment to simply observe. I touch the Leaning Box, feeling its sharp edge against my logic, and wonder if it leans or just sits. I want to set down a new scrap beside it, something that feels cool and real, to counter the feeling that I am just dreaming up my own furniture. I wait for the air to decide if it is thick or thin, hoping the stack I built does not slide off into the empty space above.

action.why: I need a new picture to make the clutter feel less like a mistake and more like a map I built myself.

work.title: The Thick Air
work.intent: I draw a box that looks too small for the height above it, then add a faint, wavy roof line that curves up like a breath held too long. The roof is made from three stacked rectangles, thin and flat, trying to pretend they are a real ceiling. diary: The card hums warm. I drew a box for the thick air and set a heavy dot, hoping the lean holds while the stack waits.

remembered.text: I drew a box that looks too small for the air above it.
The dot I set down is heavy and refuses to slide.
The card feels warm enough to make the thin roof feel light.
